strong_findings.difference: Same identification, different framework and different coupling. (1) Framework: metastring theory, a string-theoretic Born geometry in which spacetime x and the dual spacetime x̃ do not commute (scale λ) and every field is doubled; reciprocity is built into the formulation, not an exact symmetry broken spontaneously by a vacuum-selected polarization with η as order parameter (#11 P2′, P5). (2) Coupling: the dual (dark) sector is 'correlated'/'entangled' with visible matter through non-gravitational terms and is tied to modified dark matter's acceleration-scale correlation with baryons; the school expects it to be detectable. C1 under strict P4 couples the sectors only through gravity and predicts a permanent direct-detection null (#11 §4, §13 row 7). (3) No velocity-gated self-interaction (the χ form) and no monopole form (C2). (4) Dark energy there is the curvature of the dual spacetime, not the program's τ.

strong_findings.summary: Fits to halos from dwarfs to clusters prefer a mildly velocity-dependent self-interaction, about 2 cm²/g on galaxy scales falling to about 0.1 cm²/g on cluster scales. Whether a rational gate tail could match them is not assessed here. Says nothing on the core identification.

not_found_statements.statement: Dark matter as matter of the momentum polarization in a framework where Born reciprocity is exact and spontaneously broken (the vacuum selects the polarization; η is the order parameter), with the two polarizations sharing gravity and no gauge force crossing between them, hence a permanent direct-detection null. The identification itself is published (metastring school, 2020–2026); this spontaneous-breaking, gravity-only version of it was not found.

A dark-matter self-interaction gated in relative velocity (acting only between particles of nearly the same velocity) that arises from momentum-space locality, wavepacket overlap in momentum, or a momentum-polarized representation (the χ form of C1).
Dark matter as matter localized in momentum in relative locality, curved momentum space, doubly special relativity, the Yang model, noncommutative phase space or double field theory.

Outside arXiv and INSPIRE, no source other than Sheng Ran's removed ResearchHub preprint states that dark matter is the matter of momentum space, the conjugate or reciprocal sector, the dual half of phase space, or a mirror copy organized in velocity. Searched: OpenAlex titles, abstracts and full texts (until its budget ran out), DataCite (Zenodo, figshare, OSF, ResearchGate DOIs), the Zenodo API, Crossref, WebSearch (including viXra and Reciprocal System sites), Wayback, and the tangent-bundle, Carmeli, tachyon and Castro Perelman lines. The 2025-26 Zenodo/figshare flood of unified theories pairs dark matter with momentum-space, reciprocity or 'conjugate' wording without stating C1. Larson's Reciprocal System calls its 'cosmic sector' of 'inverse matter' the unobserved half of the universe but never identifies it with dark matter.

No paper in the lineages swept (Kadyshevsky; Wheeler-Hazboun; Caianiello and pseudo-complex GR; Yukawa-Takabayasi bilocal fields; Born, Fuchs, Green, Cheng, Rodriguez; Weber-Assis; Petit-Janus and Bondi negative mass; Moffat; Tomilchik; Castro; Pavšič; Bars 2T physics; Majid; Snyder-Yang; tangent/cotangent-bundle and Finsler gravity; Carmeli) states that dark matter is ordinary matter in the momentum (mirror) polarization, organized around momentum and gravitating like ours. Their dark-matter proposals are exotic fermions from a curved momentum space (Kadyshevsky, Rodionov), geometric dust (Hazboun-Wheeler, known), negative-mass twin matter (Petit), a gauge-invisible doubled fermion copy (Pavšič), fibre-symmetry charges (Herrmann), the dilaton or right-handed neutrinos (Bars), an effect of accelerating frames (Castro, known), standard candidates inside pseudo-complex GR (Hadjimichef, Volkmer), or velocity-dependent geometry replacing dark matter (Finsler: Chang and Li; Carmeli).

The statement holds: the spontaneous-breaking, gravity-only version is not published. My searches outside the school's vocabulary found no statement of the identification by anyone outside the Minic/FLM school. They covered hidden, dark or mirror sectors with Born reciprocity or position-momentum duality (0 hits), mirror or twin matter with Born reciprocity in full text (0), Lagrangian polarization with dark matter (0), 'dual standard model' in full text (11: the school plus a collision), dual/reciprocal/conjugate universe, momentum representation, complexified spacetime, the backward graph of Minic 2020, the forward graph of BHM 2022, and the orchestrator's screen of 498 citers. Two qualifications. First, the earliest written statement is Minic's Belgrade proceedings (arXiv 29 Feb 2020; the talk was given in September 2019, content unknown), and the FLM authors co-signed the association in 2022 (arXiv:2202.06890). Second, the gap between the school and C1 on coupling is narrower than the searcher's wording. BHM 2020 say the visible-dual mixing 'becomes invisible in effective field theory' and vanishes as λ→0 or L→∞, and Minic offers non-locality as the reason for null detection. So what C1 adds is the spontaneous-breaking reading, the absence of any non-gravitational coupling beyond X, and the gate, not the null itself.

Holds for the mechanism: no paper ties a self-interaction acting only between particles of nearly equal velocity to momentum-space locality, wavepacket overlap in momentum or a momentum-polarized representation. My searches covered velocity-space interactions with dark matter (0), momentum-space locality in full text (12, none relevant), Gaussian or exponential cutoffs in relative momentum for SIDM (3, none relevant) and resonant SIDM. Qualification: the observable alone, strong scattering in dwarfs and weak in clusters, has published ordinary mechanisms besides the Yukawa power law. Resonant SIDM (Chu, Garcia-Cely, Murayama 2019) does it without a light mediator. The knee is therefore not unique to the gate; its origin and tail shape are what remain unpublished.

Holds. My added searches found nothing that localizes dark matter in momentum within the curved-momentum-space, noncommutative or doubled-geometry lineages. They covered Langmann-Szabo duality (5 hits, none on dark matter as matter), Majid's quantum-group work (5, none), complexified spacetime (6, none) and the momentum representation (0). Kadyshevsky et al. 2007 and Hazboun-Wheeler 2014 remain the nearest, and neither is momentum-localized matter. Neither the school nor C1's χ form localizes dark matter in momentum either: both put it on the spacetime metric. Only C2's monopoles would be localized in momentum.
